newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 3.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
IRISH INDEPENDENT
- The Irish general election will be a tight fight, according to the latest opinion poll.

- A summer of sporting spectactulars will net close to 100 million Irish pounds next year for Ireland with the start of the Tour de France, the World Equestrian Games and the Cutty Sark Tall Ships ensuring world wide media attention.
- The poultry industry in the Republic of Ireland was on high alert on Wednesday night amid fears of an outbreak of deadly Newcastly disease on a Cavan farm.
- The Dublin equity market regained some of its composure on Wednesday after the heavy setback on Tuesday.
- The Irish pound fell against major currencies again on Wednesday as analysts swung round to the view that the currency may be headed for a general depreciation in coming months.
IRISH TIMES
- The gap between the two options for government is steadily closing within weeks of the expected general election, according to the lastest opinion poll.
- The 1998 Tour de France will start in Dublin. The official announcement of an Irish start to the world-famous cycle race will be made in Dublin later today.
- Almost 1,250 new jobs in 17 projects backed by Ireland's state development board, IDA, around the country were announced yesterday.
- Irish police investigating the murder of journalist Veronica Guerin expect to arrest up to three more people by the end of the week.
- Despite continuing speculation on an IRA ceasefire, the British Defence Secretary said there was little prospect of a ceasefire before the British general election.
- Irish share prices are facing further sharp losses after the U.S. stock market took another dive last night.
- The Irish pound has fallen back below the crucial 10 per cent level in the ERM grid.
- Passenger numbers through London City Airport during March were up 69 per cent on March of last year.
EXAMINER

- The Irish government's growing election confidence received a further boost last night with the latest opinion poll showing that it has sharply closed the lead enjoyed for months by the main opposition parties, Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats.
- Ireland's World Cup qualification hopes slumped disastrously in bitterly cold Skopje yesterday when Macedonia scored a surprise 3-2 win.
